findings.title: Team administrators are rejected by the authorization check
findings.body: The team-role condition requires the actor to be both a team admin and a team owner. These are alternative membership roles, so ordinary team administrators (and, depending on the role query semantics, owners) receive FORBIDDEN even though they are intended to manage team bookings. This should use an OR check, consistent with the `isTeamAdminOrOwner` permission represented elsewhere in the bookings UI.

findings.title: Guest addresses are not canonically deduplicated or compared to the blacklist
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` compares raw email strings only against the pre-existing attendees and does not deduplicate entries within `guests`. In particular, the blacklist is lowercased at lines 70-72 while submitted addresses are not, so a blacklisted address can bypass the policy by changing case. A request containing the same new address twice also sends both rows to `createMany`, producing duplicate attendees when no database constraint exists or failing the whole batch when one does. Normalize addresses before blacklist/existing-attendee checks and deduplicate them server-side.

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before calendar synchronization succeeds
findings.body: The attendee records are committed before `updateCalendarAttendees` is called. If the calendar provider update fails, the mutation returns an error but the guests remain in the booking. Retrying the same request then finds those guests in `booking.attendees` and rejects it as having no unique guests, leaving the organizer calendar and the booking permanently out of sync through this workflow. Use a compensating rollback/durable retry strategy or otherwise make the external synchronization recoverable after the database write.

findings.title: Calendar updates use the guest-adder's credentials instead of the booking owner's
findings.body: The mutation explicitly authorizes attendees and team admins to add guests, but it builds `EventManager` with credentials fetched for `ctx.user`, the person performing the action. The booking's calendar references and destination calendar normally belong to `booking.user` (whose credentials are loaded at lines 35-40 but never used). Thus an attendee or team admin will attempt the update with an unrelated account's credentials, so the organizer's connected calendar cannot be updated reliably. Use the booking organizer/calendar owner's credentials for this update.

findings.title: Notification classification uses requested guests rather than inserted guests
findings.body: The database operation inserts only `uniqueGuests`, but the email call receives the original `guests` input. For example, when a request contains one already-attending address and one new address, the existing attendee is not inserted but `sendAddGuestsEmails` treats them as a new guest and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` with a confirmed calendar invite. Pass the actual inserted guest list (`uniqueGuests`) to avoid sending incorrect new-booking emails.

findings.title: The mutation can add guests to cancelled or rejected bookings
findings.body: After loading the booking, the handler checks only existence and authorization; it never validates its lifecycle status. An authorized caller can invoke this endpoint directly for a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or PENDING booking, which inserts attendees and sends calendar/email payloads hardcoded as `CONFIRMED`. This can revive a cancelled appointment in recipients' calendars or invite people to an appointment that was never accepted. Reject non-accepted bookings (and enforce the condition atomically with the update if cancellation can race).

findings.title: Guest-addition emails bypass disabled standard-email settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally queues organizer and attendee messages and does not accept or check the event type metadata. Consequently, events configured with `disableStandardEmails` still send guest-addition notifications, unlike the adjacent location-change and scheduled-email paths. Thread the event metadata into this helper and honor the host and attendee suppression flags before enqueueing messages.

findings.title: Team members are never included in guest-addition notifications
findings.body: The constructed `CalendarEvent` never sets `team`, and `eventType: true` does not load Prisma's `EventType.team` relation or its members. As a result, `calendarEvent.team?.members` is always absent in `sendAddGuestsEmails`, making its team-member notification loop unreachable for this endpoint. Team booking members therefore do not receive the guest-addition update; load the team and members and include them in the calendar event.
